title: Why Is Tank Armor Slanted?
description:
In nineteen forty one, German soldiers met a Soviet tank their guns could barely hurt. Its armor was not especially thick. But it was tilted, slanted back at a steep angle, and shells that should have gone through bounced off. That tank was the T thirty four, and its sloped armor changed tank design for decades. Today, eleven parts of a tank, and why each one exists, starting with that angle.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 11 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:09 1. The slanted front plate
2:22 2. The wedge on the turret
3:32 3. The secret layers inside
4:48 4. The bricks that explode
6:01 5. The cage around the tank
7:12 6. The roof panels that blow off
8:19 7. The engine in the front
9:24 8. The periscopes
10:30 9. The tubes on the turret
11:30 10. The wide tracks
12:32 11. The radar that shoots back
13:45 The verdict

Sources:
- Sloped armour (effective thickness, ricochet, T-34 45 mm at 60°, Panther glacis 80 mm at 55°): Wikipedia, "Sloped armour" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloped_armour ; Wikipedia, "T-34" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-34 ; Wikipedia, "Panther tank" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panther_tank
- Leopard 2A5 wedge-shaped add-on armour: Wikipedia, "Leopard 2" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopard_2
- Long-rod APFSDS penetrators: Wikipedia, "Armour-piercing fin-stabilized discarding sabot" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armour-piercing_fin-stabilized_discarding_sabot
- Chobham / composite armour, depleted uranium in M1A1HA: Wikipedia, "Chobham armour" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chobham_armour ; Wikipedia, "M1 Abrams" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M1_Abrams
- Explosive reactive armour (Blazer, Lebanon 1982; Kontakt): Wikipedia, "Reactive armour" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactive_armour
- Slat armour (~50% effectiveness against RPGs), anti-drone cages: Wikipedia, "Slat armor" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slat_armor
- Abrams ammunition compartment and blowout panels: Wikipedia, "M1 Abrams"; Wikipedia, "Blow-off panel" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blow-off_panel
- Merkava front engine and rear door: Wikipedia, "Merkava" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merkava
- Periscopes and vision devices: Wikipedia, "Periscope" (military use) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periscope
- Smoke grenade dischargers, multispectral smoke, laser warning: Wikipedia, "Smoke grenade" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoke_grenade
- Tracks and ground pressure: Wikipedia, "Continuous track" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuous_track ; Wikipedia, "Ground pressure" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_pressure
- Trophy active protection (first combat interception March 2011 near Gaza; fitted to M1A2 and Leopard 2A8): Wikipedia, "Trophy (countermeasure)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trophy_(countermeasure)
